answer: A claim settles only when a real person hands this head their one live grievance and burns, once and for good, their right to be a claimant again, here or anywhere. They get the grievance carried, but lose every route to being made whole. The burn is recorded as a spiral inside the nebula of spent appeals, publicly, naming one address, not lendable to a sibling head. The scarce input is that one unrepeatable right: unprintable, gone once spent. A farm's tenth head needs a tenth person who burned theirs, so the fable at the nadir is one address holding a column, and careful people keep theirs.
